promenade.description: The Scioto Mile Promenade is the named 13.5-acre riverfront park and greenway segment at 233 Civic Center Drive, with paved paths, river frontage and downtown connections.
promenade.hours: The Promenade is open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.; events, high water, construction or maintenance can affect individual sections.
promenade.location: Navigate to the named Promenade rather than the broad Scioto Mile corridor. Its exact mapped way follows the east bank of the Scioto River beside Civic Center Drive.
promenade.parking: Use downtown garages, surface lots or metered street parking; the official visitor guide does not promise a dedicated Promenade lot.
promenade.restrooms: Permanent accessible restrooms are near the Scioto Mile fountain south of the Promenade. The operator does not list a dedicated restroom on the Promenade itself.
promenade.fees: The Promenade is free. Downtown parking, reservations, concessions and ticketed events cost separately.
promenade.accessibility: The Promenade uses broad paved paths, but the operator warns that the 175-acre Scioto Mile includes mixed terrain and long distances. Accessible parking and loading zones are listed elsewhere along the corridor.
promenade.dogs: Dogs are welcome on leash. Keep pets out of and away from the interactive fountain when continuing south along the riverfront.
promenade.family: The paved riverfront route works for family walks, but it is a linear waterfront rather than a fenced play area; supervise children near streets and the river edge.
promenade.need: Choose a turnaround point before starting. High water, festivals and construction may interrupt a longer riverfront route even while the Promenade remains generally open.
promenade.imageAlt: Paved Scioto Mile Promenade beside the Scioto River and downtown Columbus
promenade.sourceLabel: Columbus Recreation and Parks / Scioto Mile

franklin-park-conservatory.description: Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens is a separately operated, ticketed attraction at 1777 East Broad Street within Franklin Park.
franklin-park-conservatory.hours: The Conservatory is normally open daily from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., except Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day; special engagements can use different hours.
franklin-park-conservatory.location: Use the Conservatory's 1777 East Broad Street entrance, not the city park address. The exact pin is on the named Conservatory building footprint.
franklin-park-conservatory.parking: Free parking is available in Conservatory lots A and B and at the Wells Barn, with additional city-park parking nearby. A passenger drop-off is available at the entrance.
franklin-park-conservatory.restrooms: Visitor restrooms are inside the Conservatory during its operating hours. Do not assume access after the ticketed attraction closes.
franklin-park-conservatory.fees: As checked, admission including the cultural-arts fee is $25.20 for adults, $21 for seniors, $17.33 for children ages 3–12, and $4 with qualifying SNAP, EBT, WIC or Medicaid identification; members and children under 3 are free. Special engagements may differ.
franklin-park-conservatory.accessibility: The Conservatory lists paved approaches, ramps, elevators and a limited number of free wheelchairs. Contact the attraction about specific accommodations before visiting.
franklin-park-conservatory.dogs: Only service animals are allowed, including in the Conservatory's outdoor gardens; pets are not permitted.
franklin-park-conservatory.family: The Children's Garden is included with admission, but Sandstone Creek has been closed since June 17, 2026. Stroller restrictions may apply in crowded galleries or special exhibitions.
franklin-park-conservatory.need: The Palm House, Davis Showhouse and Wolfe Terrace are closed for renovation until fall 2027. Check current tickets and special-engagement hours before leaving.
franklin-park-conservatory.imageAlt: Palm House exterior at Franklin Park Conservatory
franklin-park-conservatory.sourceLabel: Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens

cascades.description: The Cascades are Franklin Park's named landscaped waterfall and lower-pond landmark, presently visible only as a closed destination while the city addresses a leak.
cascades.hours: The Cascades have been closed since June 23, 2026 because of a leak in the lower pond. The surrounding park remains open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.
cascades.location: The exact pin comes from the geotag on the destination-specific Commons photograph, south-west of the Conservatory within Franklin Park.
cascades.parking: Use the city park lots off East Broad Street or Franklin Park West; do not cross closure barriers to shorten the approach.
cascades.restrooms: The city park page does not list a dedicated restroom at the Cascades. Conservatory restrooms require access during the separately operated attraction's hours.
cascades.fees: There is no park admission, but the Cascades are currently closed. Conservatory admission and parking-related costs are separate.
cascades.accessibility: Do not assess the closed Cascades route as accessible. The park has a paved 1.1-mile path, but closure barriers and the water-feature edge govern current access.
cascades.dogs: Dogs in the surrounding city park must be securely leashed or under direct control; keep them outside the closed Cascades area and remove waste.
cascades.family: Treat this as a closed water-feature viewpoint, not a play or wading area. Keep children behind all barriers.
cascades.need: This page documents the named landmark without implying access. The city says design and repair work will follow investigation of the lower-pond leak; check the official park alert before visiting.
cascades.imageAlt: Franklin Park Cascades in a 2008 photograph, before the 2026 closure

goodale-park-pond.description: Goodale Park Pond is the park's named central water body, mapped as an active facility by Columbus Recreation and Parks and pictured with its fountain and gazebo.
goodale-park-pond.hours: The pond is within Goodale Park, which is open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.; fountain operation and event access may vary independently.
goodale-park-pond.location: The exact pin is the centroid of active water-body record 849 in the official Columbus Park Facilities layer, north-east of the Shelterhouse.
goodale-park-pond.parking: Use city lots off Park Street or Dennison Avenue, then follow park paths toward the pond. Event conditions can alter the shortest approach.
goodale-park-pond.restrooms: The park page does not list a dedicated pond restroom. Shelterhouse restrooms are for building users when that facility is open.
goodale-park-pond.fees: Viewing the pond and ordinary park use are free. Parking, reservations and permitted events cost separately.
goodale-park-pond.accessibility: Paved park paths approach the pond, but the city does not claim every edge or viewing position is barrier-free. Conditions near the open water and turf vary.
goodale-park-pond.dogs: Animals must be securely leashed or under direct control. Keep them out of the pond, respect other visitors and remove waste.
goodale-park-pond.family: The pond is an open water body, not a fenced splash area. Keep children close and away from the edge.
goodale-park-pond.need: The city identifies this feature as a pond and does not list Goodale Park among its swimming facilities. Do not treat the fountain as an invitation to enter the water.
goodale-park-pond.imageAlt: Goodale Park Pond with fountain, gazebo and mature trees

goodale-park-shelterhouse.description: Goodale Park Shelterhouse is the named 1,680-square-foot reservable venue with enclosed patios, kitchenette, restrooms and climate control.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.hours: The Shelterhouse is available by reservation Tuesday through Sunday and on holidays, with booking windows that vary by day. Requests must be submitted at least 15 days ahead.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.location: The exact pin is the centroid of active Goodale Shelterhouse record 157 in the official Columbus Park Facilities layer, on the west side of the pond.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.parking: Use the park lots off Park Street or Dennison Avenue. Confirm event setup and access details with the rental office before a reserved gathering.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.restrooms: Restrooms are inside the Shelterhouse for building users. The listing does not promise public walk-up restroom access when the building is closed or reserved.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.fees: Rental starts at $100 per hour for Columbus residents and $120 per hour for nonresidents, with minimum hours and additional fees depending on the booking.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.accessibility: The city describes the Shelterhouse as accessible. That statement applies to the venue and does not establish that every surrounding park route or surface is barrier-free.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.dogs: Animals in the surrounding park must be securely leashed or under direct control. Confirm venue rules before bringing any animal other than a service animal inside a rental.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.family: The venue accommodates up to 75 people and includes restrooms and climate control, but it is a reservable building rather than a guaranteed drop-in family facility.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.need: A reservation request is not immediate access: submit at least 15 days ahead and confirm approval, fees, setup time and building rules before planning an event.
goodale-park-shelterhouse.imageAlt: Goodale Park Shelterhouse exterior and entrance

schiller-park-pond.description: Schiller Park Pond is the city's active stocked-fishing water body west of the community center, with a footbridge and open lawn around its edge.
schiller-park-pond.hours: The pond is within Schiller Park, which is open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Fishing conditions, maintenance and future renovation work can affect use independently.
schiller-park-pond.location: The exact pin is the centroid of active stocked-pond record 867 in the official Columbus Park Facilities layer, west of the Schiller Community Center.
schiller-park-pond.parking: Use the park's documented lot by the community center at 1069 Jaeger Street or lawful neighborhood parking, then follow park paths west. Events can reduce nearby availability.
schiller-park-pond.restrooms: The reliable documented restroom opportunity is inside the Schiller Community Center during its staffed hours; the city does not list a dedicated pond restroom.
schiller-park-pond.fees: The city posts no admission charge for ordinary pond viewing or park access. Any fishing-license requirement, classes, permits or events are separate.
schiller-park-pond.accessibility: A paved park loop approaches the pond, but the city does not document every pond-edge position, bridge approach or turf surface as barrier-free.
schiller-park-pond.dogs: Animals must be securely leashed or under direct control, and handlers must remove waste. Keep dogs out of the stocked pond and clear of anglers.
schiller-park-pond.family: The pond is open water rather than a fenced play feature. Keep children close at the edge and do not infer that swimming or wading is allowed.
schiller-park-pond.need: The city's long-range program and capital budget identify future pond renovation, but they are not current closure notices. Check posted conditions and Recreation and Parks alerts before relying on fishing or bridge access.
schiller-park-pond.imageAlt: Schiller Park Pond, footbridge and surrounding lawn

schiller-statue.description: The Schiller Statue is the named 1891 bronze landmark at the west entrance, reached through Huntington Gardens from City Park Avenue.
schiller-statue.hours: The statue is outdoors within Schiller Park's daily 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. hours. Permitted ceremonies and volunteer garden work can occupy the immediate approach without creating separate public hours.
schiller-statue.location: The exact pin is the Wikidata position for the named Schiller Statue. The city calls this Site C and identifies it as the general public entrance area that must remain unobstructed.
schiller-statue.parking: Approach from lawful neighborhood parking on the City Park Avenue side for the shortest garden walk, or use the documented park lot near the community center and cross the park.
schiller-statue.restrooms: The closest reliable documented restrooms are inside the Schiller Community Center during staffed hours; the statue and Huntington Gardens do not have a listed dedicated restroom.
schiller-statue.fees: Viewing the outdoor statue has no posted admission charge. A permitted wedding site or organized event requires separate approval and fees.
schiller-statue.accessibility: The statue is approached by Huntington Gardens' brick promenade, but neither the city nor garden partner documents every curb, grade or surface transition as barrier-free.
schiller-statue.dogs: Animals must be securely leashed or under direct control and waste must be removed. Keep dogs out of the perennial beds and yield to permitted gatherings.
schiller-statue.family: This is a quiet public-art and garden stop rather than a play feature. Children can view the statue and engraved promenade while staying out of planted beds.
schiller-statue.need: The statue area is a reservable wedding site, but city rules say the park stays public and the general entrance cannot be blocked. Volunteer garden work occurs Tuesday evenings and Saturday mornings, so share the narrow approach courteously.
schiller-statue.imageAlt: Friedrich Schiller statue above the west entrance garden beds

columbus-park-of-roses.description: Columbus Park of Roses is the named 13-acre public garden within Whetstone Park, with five garden areas, more than 350 rose varieties and a separate dusk closing time.
columbus-park-of-roses.hours: Columbus Park of Roses is open from 7:00 a.m. to dusk year-round, which is earlier than Whetstone Park's 11:00 p.m. closing time.
columbus-park-of-roses.location: The exact pin is on the named OpenStreetMap garden way. Enter Whetstone Park on Hollenback Road and continue about one-half mile west; the gardens are east of the Shelterhouse at the top of the steps.
columbus-park-of-roses.parking: Free garden parking is reached from Hollenback Road. Step-free ADA parking is at the garden's east end off Roselea Place; check construction notices before relying on the usual route.
columbus-park-of-roses.restrooms: Portable restrooms are at the east end beside ADA parking and north of the Shelterhouse near the Backyard Garden. Shelterhouse indoor restrooms are for event users.
columbus-park-of-roses.fees: There is no admission fee and ordinary visitor parking is free. Shelterhouse rentals, wedding sites and special activities cost separately.
columbus-park-of-roses.accessibility: Use the ADA parking at the east end off Roselea Place for a step-free approach. The operator does not describe every garden path, lawn or construction segment as barrier-free.
columbus-park-of-roses.dogs: Dogs in city parks must be securely leashed or under direct control and waste must be removed. Keep animals out of formal beds and yield to garden work and events.
columbus-park-of-roses.family: The free outdoor garden works for a short family walk, but it is a planted landscape rather than a playground. Keep children on paths and out of beds and water features.
columbus-park-of-roses.need: The strongest rose display generally begins in mid-June and lasts through mid-September. Weather shifts bloom, and 2026 hard-surface and Hollenback Road work may temporarily alter paths or parking.
columbus-park-of-roses.imageAlt: Rose beds and fountain at Columbus Park of Roses during summer bloom
